title: The Security Of Practical Post-selection In Gaussian-modulated Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 September 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes the security of practical post-selection techniques in Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD).
motivation: Post-selection can improve the performance of CV-QKD, but its practical security implications need rigorous analysis to ensure real-world implementations remain secure against eavesdropping.
method: The authors develop a security proof for Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD with post-selection, likely using composable security frameworks or entropic bounds to limit the eavesdropper's information.
result: They derive security conditions and key-rate bounds for practical post-selection, identifying parameter regimes where secure key generation is achievable.
conclusion: The work provides a security foundation for practical post-selection in CV-QKD, supporting its safe deployment in quantum networks.

title: Ten-second Electron-spin Coherence In Isotopically Engineered Diamond
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 September 2026;
tldr: Researchers achieve ten-second electron-spin coherence in isotopically engineered diamond, likely using nitrogen-vacancy centers.
motivation: Long electron-spin coherence times are essential for quantum memories, sensors, and quantum information processing with colour centres.
method: Isotopically engineer diamond (e.g., purified 12C) to suppress nuclear spin noise and measure electron-spin coherence via Ramsey or Hahn echo techniques at cryogenic temperatures.
result: A coherence time of ten seconds is observed, significantly extending the state of the art for electron spins in diamond.
conclusion: This advance establishes isotopically engineered diamond as a leading platform for long-lived quantum memories and spin-based quantum technologies.

title: The Equivalence Of Quantum Deletion And Insertion Errors On Permutation-invariant Codes
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 October 2026;
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between quantum deletion and insertion errors on permutation-invariant codes.
motivation: Quantum error correction against synchronization errors such as insertions and deletions is important for reliable quantum information processing, but the relationship between these two error types has been unclear.
method: The authors analyze permutation-invariant quantum codes under deletion and insertion channels, showing a transformation or equivalence between the two error models.
result: They prove that deletion errors and insertion errors are equivalent on permutation-invariant codes, implying correction capabilities transfer between them.
conclusion: This equivalence simplifies the design and analysis of quantum codes for synchronization errors and highlights permutation-invariant codes as a useful framework.

title: Unitary Fault-tolerant Encoding Of Pauli States In Surface Codes
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 October 2026;
tldr: The paper presents a unitary fault-tolerant method for encoding Pauli states in surface codes, enabling efficient logical state preparation for quantum error correction.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires reliable preparation of logical states in surface codes, but existing encoding schemes can be resource-intensive or non-unitary.
method: The authors develop a unitary fault-tolerant encoding of Pauli states in surface codes, likely using code deformation or lattice surgery techniques to implement logical state preparation within the stabilizer formalism.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant encoding of Pauli states with unitary operations, potentially reducing resource overhead and improving compatibility with surface code architectures.
conclusion: This work contributes a practical method for logical state initialization in surface codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: High-order Magnus Expansion For Hamiltonian Simulation
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 October 2026;
tldr: The paper develops high-order Magnus expansion methods to improve the accuracy and efficiency of Hamiltonian simulation, a central algorithmic primitive in quantum computing.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key application of quantum computers, but high-order numerical integrators for time-dependent Hamiltonians are needed to reduce gate counts and discretization error.
method: The authors construct and analyze high-order Magnus expansion schemes for simulating time-dependent Hamiltonians, providing rigorous error bounds and complexity analysis of the resulting quantum circuits/discrete approximations.
result: The proposed high-order Magnus schemes achieve improved error scaling with respect to the simulation time and step size compared to standard product-formula approaches, yielding more efficient Hamiltonian simulation.
conclusion: High-order Magnus expansions provide a promising route to accurate and resource-efficient Hamiltonian simulation, though the work primarily advances numerical algorithm design rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic questions.

title: Demonstration Of Subspace-search Variational Quantum Eigensolver Using Photonic Orbital Angular Momentum Qudits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 October 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates a subspace-search variational quantum eigensolver using photonic orbital angular momentum qudits.
motivation: Variational quantum eigensolvers are promising for near-term quantum devices, and qudits may offer advantages over qubits for certain algorithms.
method: Implements the subspace-search variational quantum eigensolver on a photonic platform that encodes quantum information in the orbital angular momentum of photons as qudits.
result: Successfully demonstrates the eigensolver's ability to find eigenvalues and eigenvectors within a target subspace using the photonic qudit setup.
conclusion: The work shows that photonic orbital angular momentum qudits are a viable platform for variational quantum algorithms, though the contribution is primarily an experimental implementation of a known algorithm.

title: Anomalous Weak Values In A Generalized Mach–Zehnder Interferometer Extracted Directly From Intensity Measurements
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 September 2026;
tldr: The paper reports a generalized Mach–Zehnder interferometer scheme for extracting anomalous weak values directly from intensity measurements.
motivation: Weak values are central to quantum measurement foundations and metrology, but their direct extraction from raw intensities may simplify experiments and reveal anomalous effects.
method: A generalized Mach–Zehnder interferometer is used, and the anomalous weak values are inferred from measured light intensities rather than from full tomographic reconstruction.
result: Anomalous weak values are observed and extracted directly from intensity data in the interferometric setup.
conclusion: The intensity-based approach provides a practical route to accessing weak-value phenomena, though its connection to the researcher's core quantum information and thermodynamics interests is limited.

title: Breaking Rayleigh’s Curse: Broadband Frequency Super-resolution Via A Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 October 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes using a quantum harmonic oscillator to achieve broadband frequency super-resolution, overcoming Rayleigh's curse.
motivation: Rayleigh's curse limits the resolution of closely spaced frequencies in spectroscopy and sensing, and quantum resources can surpass classical limits.
method: The approach likely employs a quantum harmonic oscillator as a probe, measuring its response to broadband frequency signals to extract super-resolved spectra.
result: The method demonstrates super-resolution beyond the Rayleigh limit over a broad frequency range.
conclusion: Quantum harmonic oscillators provide a viable platform for broadband frequency super-resolution, with potential applications in spectroscopy and quantum sensing.
